english:
Praise be to the Holy Mother and to Jesus Christ. My name is Tina. I am from a place called Muvattupuzha.
I came to know about Kreupasanam, but I am not someone who usually travels this way. Even though my mother’s home is in Ernakulam, I had never come this side before. When I was in America,
a sister there told me, “Tina, when you go to your native place, make sure to go to Kreupasanam. You must go to Mother, especially with your child.”
At that time, I didn’t take it too seriously because, even though I go to church and my elder sister is a nun, I was not a person of very strong faith.
After I came back to my native place and some time had passed, I started getting severe headaches. I didn’t particularly consult any doctors.
I was just buying some painkillers from the medical shop and taking them. Then, it reached a point where I couldn’t drive because my left side
became completely blind. To find out what it was, I consulted an ophthalmologist. After the doctor did all the tests on my eyes, the doctor
said, “Tina, this is not an issue with your eyes. Something has affected your nerves, and that’s why you’re facing this problem.” So, the doctor advised me to consult a neurologist. Then the doctor
himself referred me to a specialist. When I consulted that doctor, he said, “Only after taking an MRI can we know exactly what it is.”
After taking the MRI, the doctor said, “Tina, this is a brain tumor. It’s at a stage where survival, or even if surgery is done, recovery is not possible.”
Because, in what is called meningioma, there are three stages — if it’s stage one or two, we can do an open surgery or a keyhole surgery and recover. But mine—
was the third stage — stage three. The doctor said even if it recovers, one side of my body will be completely paralyzed, or my eyesight will be totally lost, or
my memory will be completely gone. There was no other option. If surgery wasn’t done, within two to three months, I would be dead — that’s what the doctor said. Then he said
it was my choice whether to go ahead with the surgery or not. I thought, anyway, all of us have to die one day. So instead of going through all that pain from surgery,
I thought I would just go home to be with my child. I didn’t want to be a burden to my family, so I decided not to do the surgery.
My dad’s sister, Rincy aunty, is someone who comes here every month, takes the covenant, and prays. Aunty told me, “Tina, if you have faith, I will take you to Kreupasanam. If you pray and truly believe, you will be saved from this.”
That’s how, for the first time, I came here last year, on August 26. I came in the morning, took the covenant. My baby was very small then — just one and a half years old.
I brought him along and took the covenant. Honestly, until I took that covenant, I didn’t have faith. That’s the truth. But after taking the covenant and listening to Father’s talks,
I gained faith. I felt that even if I had the operation, I would recover. With that faith, I went back. When I met the doctor and told him to fix the date for surgery, the doctor said,
“Tina, this isn’t something we can wait on. It’s better if you get admitted today itself.” So, I got admitted that very day.
The next day was a Monday when I was admitted to the hospital. My surgery was scheduled for Wednesday, January 26. Before the surgery, the doctor told me, “Tina,
there won’t be a complete recovery. Only after opening up can we see the exact position of it. If any vein or anything is damaged during the process,
we can’t say now what will happen to you — we can only tell after the surgery.” Then the doctor told me, “If there’s anyone you want to meet, you can meet them now.”
The previous day, Father came and gave me the anointing of the sick. I think I must have been the youngest person to receive the last rites at such a young age — I don’t know. Anyway,
I faced that surgery seeing death right in front of me. That morning, at seven o’clock, I was taken into the operation theatre. I had the covenant medal from here in my hand. The doctor,
whose name was Dr. Tom Jose, was there. I told the doctor, “Doctor, I have only one request. Please allow me to keep this covenant medal in the operation theatre and also near me on the ventilator
after the surgery.” The doctor said, “Okay, Tina, no issue. You can give it to the sister there, and she’ll place it in the right spot.” Since it had a metal part, they removed that portion and told me to hand it over to the sister.
So before entering the operation theatre, I gave the medal to the sister there, and then I went in. The surgery that was supposed to take five hours actually took nine hours to complete.
We also needed six bottles of blood for the operation. At the last minute, there was a shortage of blood, but as I said, by Mother’s great blessing,
we unexpectedly got the required blood at the exact right time — from people we didn’t even know, through some group connections. So, the surgery was completed. I was on the ventilator for two days,
and by the time I was shifted to the ICU, I regained consciousness. Even then, I didn’t feel any particular excitement. The doctor asked me, “Tina, can you hear me?” I said, “Yes, I can hear.” “Can you see?” “Yes, I can see.”
I moved my hands and legs a little — everything was fine. I couldn’t move my head because of the surgery, also all my hair had been completely shaved off for the open surgery. The hair I have now is my second growth.
But I could see, hear, and move after the surgery — I had no issues at all. This was purely by the blessing of Mother, because from such a condition,
no human expected me to recover. I had shown myself to three hospitals for second opinions, including one in the U.S. All of them said,
“Tina, the stage has already advanced. Surgery is the only option now, but 100% recovery will not be possible.” From that condition,
If today I am able to drive and come here and stand before you to share my testimony, it is only by the blessing of the Holy Mother. I am standing here purely because of her grace. I was
an air hostess — part of the crew with Indian Airlines. Now, I can’t return to that same field because it was a major surgery. But I am currently working at Infopark,
in the IT profession. For this great blessing, I thank the Holy Mother a hundred thousand times. After I took the covenant and returned home, as the sister here instructed, I applied
the covenant oil on my forehead every single day without fail — except for the days I was on the ventilator. Even when I was in the ICU, I never missed it. Then, because of
my health issues, I couldn’t eat solid food — I could only take light, liquid foods. So when I ate things like porridge or soft rice gruel,
I always added the blessed salt from here. As a result of all that, I recovered so quickly. Earlier, I was not a person who was very active in church or involved much in charity work.
But after this surgery, I started going to church regularly whenever I could, praying, and doing whatever acts of charity I was able to do for others. All this, I firmly believe,
is only through the blessing of the Holy Mother. Jeremiah 30:13–14, 17 says: “There is no one to plead your cause; there is no remedy for your wound; you will not be healed.
All your loved ones have forgotten you; they do not care for you. But I will restore you to health and heal your wounds,” declares the Lord.
Tina Bobby — this daughter — went through the most severe illness of her life, and it was through meeting the Holy Mother through the Kreupasanam Marian Covenant that
…she entered into the covenant life — a life of complete prayer and surrender, trusting entirely in the Mother. She regularly used the covenant articles — the covenant oil and the covenant salt —
and kept the covenant medal close to her throughout all the days of her illness, offering her life completely to the Mother and praying with full faith.
Through that prayer and surrender, this daughter testifies at this altar to the miraculous healing she received. Dear ones, if we are willing to hand over our life — even one that has reached the verge of death —
into the hands of the Mother, she will receive it and obtain blessings for us from her Divine Son. There is only one thing the Mother desires from us —
we should not live as we did before. We must decide to live a new life — a life that knows God, offers our soul to Him, and is strengthened in faith. The daughter says, as she stands near her Mother,
with tears of gratitude for the new life she has been given: what we call impossible, the Covenant Mother makes possible. What we think is hopeless, the Covenant Mother turns into blessing.
When doctors say there is no life left, and count our months, the Covenant Mother extends our years by multiples — because the Covenant Mother,
standing beside her Divine Son, intercedes for us through the prayers of millions and through the grace-filled spirituality of Father Joseph. She grants us the grace to give our souls to Jesus
and begin a new life. Let us now, with grateful hearts and clapping hands, offer thanks to the Holy Mother and her Divine Son for this daughter’s miraculous healing and deep spiritual awakening.
